rationale: The stage decorations, checkerboard covering, and floorboards remain distinct. Visible grain and mild softness affect the room, especially darker areas, while the main scene remains readable and its brighter surfaces retain detail.

Grain is visible across the skin, curtains, and clothing, and facial and hair details are softened. The eyes, face outline, and fingers remain clearly identifiable, supporting the stated limitation in fine detail.

Building outlines, exposure, and colors are readable, and texture detail is reduced. However, dense colored grain covers the sky, white walls, and shaded building surfaces; calling this noise mild materially understates its pervasive visibility.

The foreground lumber grain, dirt clumps, and pipes are distinguishable. Deep shade conceals portions of the trunks and ground, while the large bright sky area is nearly white and featureless, supporting the identified exposure limitations.

The package appears dim and visibly grainy, with softened lettering and blurred food illustration details. Smaller text is difficult to resolve, so the stated effects of noise and soft focus are supported.

Strong blur softens the package boundary and lettering throughout, while conspicuous grain covers the background and package. The large brand remains recognizable, but smaller print and food details are smeared and difficult to inspect.

Balcony lines, windows, boats, and individual water ripples are clearly resolved. The blue sky and water retain smooth or naturally textured appearance, with readable highlights and no conspicuous compression blocks or processing artifacts.

All four jets have distinct silhouettes, legible canopy and tail markings, and sufficient contrast against the smooth gray sky. Fine detail is slightly soft, but there is no conspicuous grain or blur that impairs the aircraft.
